What It Is: Built-in or custom shortcut commands that trigger specific Claude Code behaviors
When It Runs: On-demand — only when explicitly invoked by the user
How to Invoke: Type /command-name in the Claude Code prompt
Persistence: Session-scoped or stored in CLAUDE.md / settings
column10: /commit — stages and commits changes with a generated message

What It Is: Shell commands that run automatically in response to lifecycle events in Claude Code
Persistence: Not invoked manually — fires based on configured event triggers
column11: Run eslint after every file edit; post a Slack message when a PR is created

What It Is: Packaged extensions that add new capabilities or integrations to Claude Code
When It Runs: Loaded at startup; features available throughout the session
How to Invoke: Enabled via configuration; features used naturally in conversation
Primary Use Case: Extending Claude Code with domain-specific tools or integrations
Example: A plugin that adds Jira ticket lookup or Figma design inspection

What It Is: Reusable prompt templates / slash command definitions that encode complex multi-step workflows
Who Defines It: Users or teams (stored as markdown files in the project or globally)
When It Runs: On-demand — invoked via a slash command shortcut
Persistence: Stored as .md files; persistent across sessions
Primary Use Case: Encoding best practices and repeatable workflows as runnable prompts
Example: /review-pr — a skill that runs a thorough PR review checklist

What It Is: External servers that expose tools and resources to Claude via a standardized protocol
When It Runs: Connected at session start; tools available throughout the conversation
How to Invoke: Claude calls MCP tools automatically when relevant to the task
Persistence: Persistent while the MCP server is running and configured
Primary Use Case: Giving Claude access to external data sources and APIs (databases
column10: An MCP server that lets Claude query a PostgreSQL database or browse the web
